summary: H.R. 7661, titled the Stop the Sexualization of Children Act, amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to prohibit the use of federal education funds for programs, activities, literature, or materials that include sexually oriented material for children under 18. The bill defines sexually oriented material to include sexually explicit conduct, gender dysphoria, or transgenderism, while explicitly carving out exceptions for standard science coursework, major world religions texts, classic literature and art, and child-trafficking security measures.

affected_groups.effect: Will not be exposed to federally funded programs, literature, or activities involving sexually oriented material, gender dysphoria, or transgenderism, while maintaining access to exempt coursework like standard science, classic literature, and anti-trafficking security education.
affected_groups.group: Students under 18 in elementary and secondary schools

affected_groups.effect: Must ensure federal funds under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 are not used to develop, host, promote, or provide prohibited materials or programs to children under 18.
affected_groups.group: Educational institutions and administrators using federal education funds

key_provisions: Prohibits the use of federal elementary and secondary education funds for programs, activities, literature, or materials for children under 18 that contain sexually oriented material.
Defines sexually oriented material as any depiction, description, or simulation of sexually explicit conduct, or material involving gender dysphoria or transgenderism.
Expressly prohibits using these funds to expose children to nude adults, stripping, or lewd or lascivious dancing.
Exempts standard science coursework (such as biology, genetics, and human anatomy) from the funding ban.

Exempts major world religions texts, classic works of literature (defined by specific lists like the Great Books of the Western World), and classic works of art (defined by Smarthistory AP Art History guides).
Exempts security measures and educational programs designed to help students recognize and respond to child sexual trafficking and grooming, including real-world legal examples.
missing_information: Specific enforcement mechanisms or penalties for non-compliance by schools or educational agencies are not mentioned in the source text.
The source text does not provide estimates of the fiscal impact or the exact number of schools and students that would alter their practices.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 7661, titled the Stop the Sexualization of Children Act, amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to prohibit the use of federal education funds for programs, activities, literature, or materials that include sexually oriented material for children under 18. The bill defines sexually oriented material to include sexually explicit conduct, gender dysphoria, or transgenderism, while explicitly carving out exceptions for standard science coursework, major world religions texts, classic literature and art, and child-trafficking security measures.
summary_detail.significance: The bill places federal restrictions on the use of education funds regarding content related to sexual topics, gender dysphoria, and transgenderism for minors under 18. Its significance depends on how schools adjust curricula and funding allocations to comply with the new federal prohibitions while utilizing the permitted educational exemptions.
